passage: Karthik met Sabina's new landlord at the tea stall near their Pune flat, and the man's face lit up so fast that Karthik's first thought was, finally, someone friendly. Raised cheeks, crinkled eyes, a full smile. The landlord even patted the plastic stool beside him. But Karthik remembered his own uncle, who felt real joy while barely changing his expression, just a small softening near the eyes. So he did not decide anything yet. Over the next few weeks he watched what the landlord did: fixed the leaking tap the same day, asked after Sabina's exams. The warm face and the warm actions matched. Karthik told Sabina that evening, "I think he is kind. But I would have believed it even if he smiled less." 🙂

qa.q: Where did Karthik meet Sabina's new landlord?
qa.a: He met the landlord at the tea stall near their Pune flat.

qa.q: Why did Karthik hold back from deciding the landlord was warm right away?
qa.a: He knew from his uncle that some people feel real pleasure with very little cheek movement, so a big smile alone was not proof either way. He waited to see whether the landlord's actions matched the smile.

qa.q: How did Karthik's approach protect him from a hasty judgement, and what could he add?
qa.a: He compared the smile with behaviour over time, like fixing the tap and asking about exams. He could also note the landlord's usual expression in calmer moments as a baseline.

qa.q: How might the landlord's smile look to someone who does not smile much themselves?
qa.a: It might feel very intense or even overdone, while for someone used to open faces it would seem ordinary and friendly.

grounding: Illustrates a young adult reading raised cheeks and crinkled eyes as warmth while knowing that expression baselines differ.

passage:
"Did you see Aanya's face when we gave her the gift?" Saurabh said, stirring his coffee. "Big cheeks, eyes all scrunched. She loved it."

"Maybe," Chetan said. "Or she was being polite."

"Come on. That is a real smile."

"It looks real. But remember Meera from accounts? She got promoted and her face barely moved. She told me later she nearly cried from happiness."

"Hmm. So no face means happy too?"

"Sometimes. Faces vary. I would say Aanya probably liked it, then wait for how she talks about it."

"Fine. I will ask her tomorrow what she actually wants next year."

Chetan laughed. "Good plan. Ask, do not just read." 🙂

qa.q: What did Saurabh notice about Aanya's face?
qa.a: He noticed big cheeks and scrunched eyes when she received the gift.

qa.q: Why did Chetan not simply accept Saurabh's reading of Aanya's smile?
qa.a: Chetan thought a real-looking smile probably meant she liked it, but he had seen Meera show great happiness with almost no facial movement. So he wanted more evidence before being sure.

qa.q: What could Saurabh do to find out whether Aanya truly liked the gift?
qa.a: He could ask her what she would like next year and listen to how she talks about the gift over the next days.

qa.q: How might Meera from accounts have felt if others assumed she was not happy about her promotion?
qa.a: She might have felt misread or a little hurt, since her joy was real but showed little on her face.

grounding: Illustrates a young adult reading raised cheeks and crinkled eyes as warmth while a friend points out that baseline expression varies.

passage: Last month I finally showed Preeti, the senior teacher on my corridor, the reading corner I'd built from old crates. She stopped in the doorway and her cheeks lifted so high her eyes almost disappeared into crinkles. "Sabina, you made this?" I felt the warmth of that before she said another word. But I've learned not to lean on that one sign. My Nani, who raised me, hardly moves her face when she's pleased. When I got this teaching job she just nodded, said "Achha," and quietly made my favourite kheer that night. So when Mr. Kulkarni, our principal, looked at the corner with an almost still face and said only "Good use of space," I didn't panic. I waited. The next week he asked me to show the other teachers how I'd built it.

qa.q: What did Sabina build the reading corner from?
qa.a: Sabina built it from old crates.

qa.q: What did Sabina feel when Mr. Kulkarni looked at the corner with an almost still face?
qa.a: Sabina may have felt a flicker of uncertainty but stayed calm and patient, because Nani had shown that pleasure can come with little movement; he might also simply have been neutral at that moment.

qa.q: What habit helped Sabina read the principal fairly?
qa.a: Sabina waited for more signs, like later actions, instead of judging from one face; the invitation to show the other teachers confirmed the approval.

qa.q: How might Nani feel if someone thought her still face meant she did not care?
qa.a: She might feel misunderstood and hurt, since she shows her pleasure through actions like making kheer rather than a big smile.

grounding: A young adult reads raised cheeks and crinkled eyes as warmth while recognising that some people show pleasure with little facial movement.

passage:
Training note, front desk, 12 March. Written by Chetan, shift supervisor.
Today I watched Dilnaz handle the morning check-outs. An older guest had left his phone charger in the room; when Dilnaz handed it back, his cheeks rose and his eyes crinkled right up. She smiled back and visibly relaxed. Easy one.
Next came Mr. Haddad, our regular, who barely changes expression. He signed his bill with a flat face and walked off. A new trainee might have worried he was unhappy. I asked Dilnaz about it afterwards. She said, "He's always like that. He greets the staff by name and comes back every month, so I don't read his face as a complaint." I agreed. She was comparing him with his own usual face, not with the smiling guest.
Next step: I've asked Dilnaz to share this at Friday's briefing for the two new trainees.

qa.q: What did Dilnaz return to the older guest?
qa.a: His phone charger, which he had left in the room.

qa.q: What did Dilnaz likely feel when the older guest's cheeks rose and his eyes crinkled?
qa.a: She likely felt relieved and warm 😊, reading it as genuine thanks; it could also have been polite courtesy, but it fit the moment.

qa.q: How could Chetan use what Dilnaz noticed to help the new trainees?
qa.a: By having Dilnaz explain at Friday's briefing that each regular has their own usual face, so trainees compare a person with themselves, not with the most smiley guest.

qa.q: How might Mr. Haddad feel if staff treated his flat face as displeasure?
qa.a: He might feel awkward or misread, fussed over for a problem he doesn't have, when his monthly visits show he is content.

grounding: Shows a young adult reading cheek-raising as warmth while knowing that a regular guest's still face is his normal baseline, not displeasure.

passage:
Sat, 9 pm
Cooked dinner for Reena and her brother tonight, the first proper meal in the new flat. When Reena tasted the rajma her cheeks went right up and her eyes crinkled at the corners. "Harsha, you liar, you said you can't cook!" Easy to read. Pure warmth. 😊
Her brother Dev was harder. Same food, face nearly still, one small nod. For a minute my stomach dropped. Did he hate it? Then he took a third helping and asked for the recipe on his way out. Reena laughed and said Dev smiles about twice a year, even at weddings.
Note to self: crinkly-eyed cheeks are a good sign, but no crinkles doesn't mean a bad one. Everyone has their own normal face, and I only know Reena's so far.

qa.q: What dish did Reena taste?
qa.a: The rajma.

qa.q: How did Harsha feel when Dev's face stayed nearly still?
qa.a: Harsha felt a drop of worry and self-doubt, wondering whether Dev hated the food; the third helping suggested Dev simply has a still face.

qa.q: What rule of thumb did Harsha take from the evening, and why is it sensible?
qa.a: That crinkly-eyed cheeks are a good sign but their absence isn't a bad one, because people have different normal faces and actions also show pleasure.

qa.q: How might Dev see the dinner, going by what he did?
qa.a: Dev likely enjoyed it, since he took a third helping and asked for the recipe, even though his face barely showed it.

grounding: A young adult reads a friend's raised cheeks and crinkled eyes as warmth and learns that another person's still face can still mean pleasure.

qa.q: What could Shankar watch for when someone's face stays still?
